newsitem.title: INDIA: New India bond traded at 100.70 rupees -dealers.
newsitem.headline: New India bond traded at 100.70 rupees -dealers.

text.p: The newly auctioned 10.85 percent 2001 bond was traded at 100.70 rupees in mid-morning trade Tuesday and dealers said prices of other securities are seen firming up.
The 10.85 percent 2001 bond was auctioned on Monday at par.
Shortly after the auction results were announced late Monday night, the bond was traded at 100.80 rupees for next-day value.
Dealers said they expect trade to be brisk on Tuesday.
"The new bond was quoted at a premium of 50 paise in the morning but this has gone up to 70 paise already," said the chief money market dealer at a private bank.

"As the price of the new bond goes up, we will see an upward realignment in prices of securities with tenures above 2001," he said. "At the moment little trade has taken place but interest is building up."
In other stocks, the 12.14 percent 2000 rose to 104.45 rupees from Monday's 104.32, the 12.59 percent 2004 to 105.52 from 105.08 and the 11.83 percent 2003 rose to 102.44 from 102.
